rules: A feature is verified only when every acceptance criterion has evidence: a command that passed, with its output recorded in verification.evidence.

features.title: Organization and project authorization boundaries
features.description: OIDC bearer-token authentication, organization membership with admin/engineer/viewer roles, project-scoped resource checks, service credentials, audited decisions.

Every project-scoped route resolves the project through the caller's organization; a resource id from another organization returns 404, never data.

Service credentials are stored hashed, scoped to one organization and role, and revocable.
Each allow/deny on a protected write is recorded as an audit event.
A parametrized test calls every protected route as an outsider and asserts no cross-organization data is returned.

features.title: Browser sign-in through OIDC
features.description: The web app signs users in with the organization's OIDC provider (authorization code + PKCE) and keeps the session in a secure, HttpOnly cookie.
acceptance: Authorization code flow with PKCE against a real OIDC provider; tokens never stored in browser storage.
Session cookie HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; logout clears it.
The development identity is unavailable in production builds.

evidence: bash scripts/smoke.sh --oidc (exit 0): a real OpenID Provider (panva/oidc-provider 9.13.3, an OpenID-certified implementation, run locally with RS256 keys and resource indicators) + the stack with the API in PAP_AUTH_MODE=oidc validating its JWT access tokens (issuer, audience, JWKS via discovery) + the web server in PAP_WEB_AUTH=oidc; e2e/oidc.spec.ts 3/3 in Chromium.

oidc.spec.ts: before sign-in /api/v1/me is 401 through the proxy, also with a page-chosen 'Bearer dev:mallory' header; Sign in -> provider login and consent pages -> back to the app (authorization code + PKCE S256 + state + nonce through openid-client 6.8.9); pap_session cookie httpOnly, secure and sameSite Lax; the transaction cookie is cleared; document.cookie, localStorage, sessionStorage and /auth/session contain no JWT; /api/v1/me reports the provider's issuer and subject; a forged Authorization header from page script still yields the session user; the user creates an organization and project in the UI; Sign out clears the cookie and /api/v1/me is 401 again.
oidc.spec.ts: a forged session cookie gives 401 and no user; in OIDC mode the settings page offers only identity-provider sign-in (no development form).

Unit tests (src/lib/server/auth.test.ts, 7): sealed cookies (AES-256-GCM, HKDF keys) round-trip and hide the token, refuse tampering, another key, and a transaction cookie replayed as a session; expired sessions read as none; PAP_WEB_AUTH=dev refused with PAP_ENV=production and production defaults to OIDC; short secrets, plain-http non-loopback issuers (incl. localhost.evil.example) and http issuers in production refused; return paths limited to same-site relative paths.
Dev mode unaffected: bash scripts/smoke.sh --e2e 7 passed (the 3 OIDC tests skip).
Found while wiring this: the API's issuer check was a string-prefix match (http://localhost.evil.example passed); now an exact hostname check with a parametrized test (test_auth.py).

limitations: Tested against oidc-provider, not against Keycloak, Entra ID, Okta or Auth0; any standards-conformant provider should work, but each customer IdP needs its configuration checked once.
No refresh tokens: the session ends when the access token expires (at most 8 h) and the user signs in again.
Sign-out clears the platform session only; it does not end the session at the identity provider (RP-initiated logout not implemented).
'Production' is decided at run time by PAP_ENV, not at build time: one web build serves both modes, and with PAP_ENV=production the development identity is refused by both the web server and the API.

features.title: Validated evidence upload and storage
features.description: Upload of source evidence into content-addressed, immutable storage with size limits and safe parsing.
acceptance: Uploads are streamed with a configurable byte limit; over-limit uploads are refused with 413 and leave nothing stored.

Filenames are never used as storage paths; path traversal attempts are refused or neutralised and tested.
Only declared media types are accepted (CSV, JSONL, JSON); archives are refused until archive extraction protection exists.
A local filesystem adapter implements the storage interface (Storage protocol) used by uploads and the worker.

features.title: S3-compatible artifact storage adapter
features.description: Second implementation of the Storage interface for S3-compatible object stores (SeaweedFS in Compose; any S3 in customer deployments).

One contract test run against both adapters (LocalStorage and S3Storage): content-addressed keys, write-once (same content is not written again), digest-checked reads, byte limit (TooLarge), a key that tries to leave the store is refused, the empty object.

Full evaluation with PAP_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3: both CSVs uploaded through the API land in the bucket under pap/sha256/..; the worker reads them back from S3 and runs the real engine (reported improvement, verified insufficient_evidence); the evidence bundle (events file, engine store) is written to S3.

features.title: Durable evaluation jobs
features.description: PostgreSQL-backed jobs with queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, run by a separate worker process.
acceptance: Submitting the same inputs twice returns the same job (idempotency by input checksum).
The worker claims jobs with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a lease; two workers never run one job.
A job whose worker died (lease expired) is re-queued on recovery and finishes; tested by killing a worker process.
Timeouts, bounded retries for transient errors, structured errors, and cancellation of queued and running jobs are tested.
Evaluation never runs inside an HTTP request handler.

evidence: test_jobs.py::test_full_evaluation: second identical submission returns the same job (200); comparison is 409 until a worker runs it (evaluation never runs in the HTTP handler)
test_concurrent_workers_never_claim_the_same_job: 8 concurrent claims on one queued job -> exactly 1 (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)

test_worker_recovery.py::test_killed_worker_is_recovered: worker started as a separate process, hard-killed while running the job; job left running with a stale lease; after lease expiry a new worker re-queues it and finishes it (attempts 2) with the same comparison as an uninterrupted run
test_lost_worker_cannot_write_after_recovery: a worker whose lease was taken over cannot persist results

test_cancel_queued / test_cancel_running_kills_the_engine; test_timeout_fails_after_bounded_attempts (job.timeout); test_transient_failure_is_retried_then_fails (queued, queued, failed after 3 attempts, structured error engine.start_failed); test_invalid_submissions (same release 422, foreign mapping 404, unknown task type -> failed input.task_type)

Playwright apps/web/e2e/release-flow.spec.ts against scripts/dev_stack.py (pgserver PostgreSQL 16.2, uvicorn API, worker with the pinned engine sha256:d51af06f, next start): sign in, add releases 2.14.0 and 2.15.0-rc1, upload baseline.csv and candidate.csv, add the mapping, start a paired evaluation, the page polls until the worker finishes, reported 'Improvement' and verified 'Insufficient evidence' shown, SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE label, paired panel, engine commit in provenance; filter Contradiction -> 32 episodes; open one -> conditions and the verifier's reasons. 1 passed (10.5 s).

features.title: Reproducible HTML and JSON reports
features.description: Export of a comparison as a self-contained HTML report and a machine-readable JSON report.
acceptance: The JSON report embeds input checksums, engine provenance, mapping revision and the engine outputs; generating it twice gives identical bytes.
The HTML report is rendered from the JSON report only and states the evidence class (synthetic, simulated, production).

evidence: test_reports.py (real engine run of the synthetic demo): GET report.json twice and a rebuild from the database in a fresh session give identical bytes; X-Report-SHA256 is the sha256 of those bytes; the report holds the input checksums (equal to provenance.inputs), engine provenance (commit e9ef873b), mapping name/version/spec_sha256, and every stored engine output byte for byte (raw equals the comparison endpoint's raw; raw_sha256 re-checked); 240 episodes sorted deterministically; no generation timestamp.

test_reports.py: report.html equals render_html(json.loads(report.json)) exactly; render_html takes only the parsed JSON (no session/settings/engine); the page names the JSON digest it was rendered from; states SYNTHETIC/SIMULATED/PRODUCTION EVIDENCE from evidence_class; escapes hostile labels; no script and no external resource; served with CSP default-src 'none'.
Outsider access to both report URLs returns 404 (test_reports.py and the OpenAPI-enumerated isolation sweep, which picked the two new routes up automatically).
Visual review of the HTML report at 1280 px light and 390 px dark: fixed narrow comparison cards (stacked full width) and a mobile overflow (grid items min-width 0).

Browser: release-flow.spec.ts downloads both reports from the comparison page (blob download with the caller's identity) and checks the HTML states SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE and contains the JSON's input checksum.

limitations: The report is regenerated on request rather than stored; byte identity relies on the stored rows being immutable (they are: results, episodes, mapping revisions and artifacts are write-once).

features.title: Real OpenMHS-backed demonstration
features.description: Labelled synthetic warehouse pick-and-place dataset taken through the whole workflow end to end.
acceptance: The dataset is generated by a seeded script, labelled synthetic in every file and report, and contains successes, missed grasps, drops, operator interventions, contradictions, unknowns and several scenarios for a baseline and a candidate.
Playwright drives create project -> releases -> upload -> evaluate -> compare -> episode drilldown -> export against the real API, worker and engine.
Worker restart recovery, duplicate submission, invalid artifact, unauthorized access, incompatible comparison and insufficient samples are exercised.

evidence: bash scripts/smoke.sh --e2e (exit 0, 2026-11-18): starts pgserver PostgreSQL, API, supervised worker and the built web app in var/smoke; scripts/smoke_api.py runs one real evaluation over HTTP (reported improvement, verified insufficient_evidence, synthetic, byte-identical JSON report, HTML names its JSON digest, outsider 404); then 7/7 Playwright tests pass.

release-flow.spec.ts: sign in -> create organization -> create project -> two releases -> upload two CSVs -> mapping -> paired evaluation on the real engine -> comparison (Improvement reported vs Insufficient evidence verified, SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE, engine commit) -> HTML+JSON export -> contradiction filter (32) -> episode conditions and reasons. All through the web app.

failure-paths.spec.ts through the UI: non-text upload refused with the reason; an artifact the mapping rejects (duplicate header) fails the evaluation with input.artifact_rejected and offers no report; same release on both sides cannot be submitted; an absent task type fails with input.task_type; min_known 1000 gives Insufficient evidence for both comparisons; the worker process is hard-killed (taskkill /T /F) while the job runs, the stack starts a new worker, the job finishes as attempt 2 of 3 with the same verdicts; resubmitting the same inputs returns the same evaluation (still attempt 2); a user of another organization sees 'organization not found', no episodes, and 404 on both report URLs.

Dataset: examples/manipulation-demo/generate.py (seeded) produces success, missed_grasp, drop, assist (operator intervention), scale_missing, scale_bad, late_reading and timeout cases for baseline and candidate across 5 SKUs x shelves (40 scenarios per release), every row data_origin=synthetic, plus 3 malformed rows per file.

limitations: Runs on the pgserver/uvicorn/next start stack (scripts/dev_stack.py), not Docker Compose (INF-003 needs a Docker engine).
Clean-machine install not yet checked (INF-003 / CI).

features.title: Operational observability (application instrumentation)
features.description: Structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP, Prometheus metrics for API and worker.
acceptance: Logs are JSON with request and job ids and never contain tokens or uploaded content.
Job duration, state counts and engine failures are exported as metrics.
Traces span API request -> job -> engine invocation.

evidence: test_observability.py (real API, real worker code, real engine): one trace from the submitting request (span 'POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_slug}/projects/{project_slug}/evaluations', request id attribute) to the worker's 'evaluation.job' span (same trace id, parent = the request span, continued from evaluation_jobs.trace_context across processes) to every engine process ('engine outcome verify' x240, 'engine ops ingest', 'engine ops compare', 'engine ops incidents', each a child of the job span; no paths or arguments in span attributes).

test_observability.py: every log line is one JSON object; the request line carries request_id, route template, status, duration and trace_id; job lines carry job_id and the same trace_id; no 'Bearer', no credential, and no fragment of the uploaded CSV appears in the logs; bearer tokens, JWTs and service tokens in a message are redacted; quotes in messages stay valid JSON (the old worker format string did not).

test_observability.py: /metrics exports pap_evaluation_jobs by state (read from the database at scrape time, so correct across API and worker), request durations by method/route template/status, job durations by outcome, engine invocations by command/result and engine failures by command/code; no tenant slugs or ids in labels. In production /metrics is 404 without PAP_METRICS_TOKEN and 401 with a wrong token.
Bridge: Engine.observers hook (test_engine_real.py) reports command, timing and outcome per process; an observer that raises does not change the engine result.
Real stack (smoke.sh --e2e, 7/7): 163 JSON request lines and JSON 'job finished' lines with job_id and trace_id in the stack log.
Found: FastAPI 0.163's built-in telemetry made a second server span recording concrete URL paths (tenant slugs, ids); disabled in favour of the template-only span (D-020).

limitations: No collector, Prometheus server or dashboards run yet: that is OBS-002 (needs INF-003). Spans are dropped unless OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set; the OTLP export path itself has not been exercised against a collector.
The web server (Next.js) is not instrumented; the API request span starts at the API.

features.title: Observability stack in Compose
features.description: OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus scrape configuration and starter dashboards as optional Compose services, receiving what OBS-001 emits.
acceptance: An optional Compose profile starts an OTel Collector and Prometheus; traces from a real evaluation arrive in the collector and the API and worker metrics are scraped.
Grafana/Loki/Tempo (AGPL-3.0) are only ever separate, unmodified services, never bundled into product images.

features.title: Real robot evidence through the platform (CoreSense drone flights)
features.description: Milestone B: one genuine recorded robot dataset imported through the existing evidence contract and evaluated by the pinned engine, with provenance, accounting and limits documented.
acceptance: Real recorded episodes (not simulated, not synthetic) enter through pap.mapping/1 and are evaluated by the API, worker and pinned engine; reports are kept.

Provenance (dataset DOI, license, bag and derived-file checksums), episodes processed, rejected rows, missing metadata, available measurements, the verification rule and its assumptions, claims the evidence cannot support, integration effort and reproducibility are documented.
No outcome or measurement is fabricated: missing data stays missing (unknown).

evidence: CoreSense Inspection Testbed ROSbag Dataset (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23243295, CC BY 4.0): 115 GoTo goals of 3 real Crazyflie drones in 3 bags (nominal, panel failure, double failure) extracted with the pinned OpenMHS commit's rosbag2 reader; 0 rows rejected; every goal has a terminal status, a joined waypoint and an OptiTrack sample within 50 ms (largest gap 5.9 ms).

Evaluated through the API, worker and pinned engine (examples/coresense/results): robots reported 0 of 35 waypoints failed in every condition; the motion-capture evidence shows 31/35 (nominal), 31/32 known (panel) and 32/34 known (double) waypoints outside a +-0.20 m box at the claim; both condition comparisons are insufficient_evidence (engine), correctly for these sample sizes.
Two runs of the same evaluation: identical counts, rates, intervals, verdicts and episode classes; only incident ids differ (derived from the per-run organization).
Found and fixed through this data: cancelled goals were counted as failure claims (contradictions); now classed by the evidence alone (test_outcome_class_table). Added the 'physical' evidence class.

limitations: No software revision in the dataset: the compared 'releases' are flight conditions of the same software, so nothing here is a release comparison.
The 0.20 m tolerance is the Aerostack2 default (flight configuration unpublished); the reference pose also feeds the controller; failures were induced; one host clock assumed.
Only GoTo goals are evaluated; Takeoff, Land and mission outcomes are not.
Nearest-sample rule (9/107 claimed arrivals inside the box) differs from the OpenMHS verifier's every-sample rule (4/107); both documented.

features.title: Controlled regression experiment with a no-change control (MuJoCo)
features.description: Milestone C: a known regression injected into a simulated controller, evaluated through the platform against a pre-registered design, with a negative control.
acceptance: Design, sample size and predictions committed before the held-out run.
Baseline, degraded and no-change groups from real simulation; nothing fabricated; rollouts regenerate byte for byte.
All statistics by the pinned engine; the known regression is detected, the no-change control gives no regression verdict, and failed predictions or engine limits are reported.
Automated test re-checks regeneration and the recorded verdicts.

evidence: PREREGISTRATION.md committed in 0971184 before any held-out episode; held-out run: 150 episodes per group (A 10 ms, B 50 ms, C 10 ms on independent seeds, D 20 ms), 0 rows rejected.

Engine verdicts (verified): A vs B regression (+97.3 pp [+92.6, +99.0]); A vs D regression (+21.3 pp [+15.0, +28.6]); A vs C insufficient_evidence (0/150 vs 0/150). All four predictions held; one predicted mechanism (source of A/C contradictions) did not and is reported.
Robot self-reports overstated the D regression about 4.5-fold (+96.7 pp reported vs +21.3 pp verified): 118 contradictions (robot timeout, fingertip within 2 cm).
test_mujoco_regression.py: 4 passed (byte-identical regeneration of all four groups; the three comparisons through run_pipeline and the pinned engine give the recorded verdicts and counts).
Resources: peak RSS 57.8-61.6 MB, 0.9-2.0 s CPU per 150 episodes; verdict 10-12 s per comparison.

limitations: Simulation of one idealised task; the self-report rule is written for the experiment.
D was chosen on the pilot (B was declared beforehand).
Only failure rates are compared (G-7); 'no change' cannot be established with a near-perfect baseline (G-8).

features.title: Self-hosted trial pack for an independent robotics engineer
features.description: Milestone D: a documented installation, a 30-minute exercise with an answer key, a conventional-script baseline, an evaluation form, known limitations and a pilot brief, so an engineer who has never seen the repository can attempt the evaluation and give feedback.
acceptance: One command installs a self-hosted trial with no credentials of ours; the exercise's tasks have objectively checkable answers.
A plain-Python baseline computes the same answers from the same raw data, checked against the engine by a test.
The install and the exercise are run once from a clean environment with no hidden manual steps, and the result is recorded honestly, including where the script is faster or simpler.
No feedback or reactions of an external user are invented.

evidence: Local dry run (Windows local stack, 2026-11-19): the exercise as written, driven through the UI, matched every answer in trial/expected.json (verdicts, 32 verified failures, 118 and 31 contradictions, the PHYSICAL EVIDENCE label, identical report hashes).
test_trial_baseline.py: 14 cases; the baseline script reproduces the engine's counts, Wilson intervals, difference intervals, verdicts and McNemar results on all five shipped comparisons.
Baseline script: 0.07-0.08 s per comparison against 7-18 s on the platform; recorded in trial/DRY_RUN.md as the places where the script is faster.

CI run 44458202782 on 36d60e7 (https://github.com/KNambiarDJsc/physical-ai-platform/actions/runs/44458202782), job 'trial dry run', clean ubuntu-24.04 runner, no secrets: `bash trial/start.sh` from a clean checkout to Ready in 512 s; the exercise T1-T6 through the UI matched every answer in expected.json; Part B scripts 0.03 s; `bash trial/start.sh reset` removed containers, volume and network. All four CI jobs green on that commit. Record kept in trial/dry-run-record/.
The first clean run failed: start.sh's password generation died of SIGPIPE under pipefail. Found only by the clean run; fixed in 36d60e7 (recorded in trial/DRY_RUN.md).

Docker Desktop on Windows/macOS and archive installs without GitHub access are untested.
The repository is private: the owner must grant access or send an archive. The pilot brief's contact line is blank for the owner to fill in.

features.title: Adapter SDK with W3C WoT / LabThings discovery
features.description: packages/device-sdk: one adapter interface (discover, read a property, invoke an action) and its first implementation for W3C Web of Things Thing Descriptions over HTTP, the protocol LabThings-FastAPI serves (D-027).
acceptance: Discovery, property reads and action invocation are tested against a real LabThings-FastAPI server, not a mock.
A link in a description that leaves the operator-configured endpoint is refused before any request is made.
An action the device refuses (invalid input) is reported as refused before it started, distinct from a failure during execution.
An action whose input carries a request id is marked idempotent in its capability description.

evidence: uv run pytest packages/device-sdk/tests: 5 passed against a real labthings-fastapi 0.3.0 server in a subprocess (discovery, live read, invocation with LabThings invocation polling, idempotency key detected, input refused before start = accepted:false).

test_links_outside_the_configured_endpoint_are_refused: a description pointing at 169.254.169.254 raises AdapterError and the transport asserts no other host is contacted (the only test with a fake transport: it tests the SDK's own rule).
uv run mypy packages/device-sdk/src: clean (strict); Semgrep project rules: 0 findings.

limitations: One adapter (W3C WoT over HTTP, as LabThings serves it). ROS 2, OPC UA, SiLA 2 adapters are not written.
WoT Discovery (.well-known/wot, directories) is not implemented; the LabThings /thing_descriptions/ listing and a single TD at the endpoint are.

features.title: LabThings virtual laboratory: simulated pump and balance
features.description: runtimes/virtual-lab: a syringe pump, an analytical balance and a simulation control served by labthings-fastapi 0.3.0 in its own uv project. The pump reports what it was commanded; the balance measures what physically happened; injected faults change the physics, never the report.
acceptance: Every Thing declares itself simulated, in its description and in a readable property.
Dispensing is idempotent per request id: a repeated id has no second physical effect, shown by the balance.
A fault (e.g. partial blockage) leaves the pump's report unchanged while the balance reading shows the shortfall.
The lab starts with the local stack (scripts/dev_stack.py) so the platform can be tried without hardware.

evidence: Same SDK tests: every Thing has a read-only simulated=true property; a repeated request id leaves the balance reading unchanged (noise only); partial_blockage leaves the pump's report at 100 µL while the balance reads 0.055-0.070 g.
smoke.sh --e2e (2026-11-21): dev_stack.py started the lab on its own port and the browser suite (21 passed) used it, including the fault-injection test.

pip-audit on runtimes/virtual-lab/uv.lock: no known vulnerabilities. Docker Compose service and image added (non-root uid 10002, read-only root, settings in /tmp); not yet built on CI (local Docker is not running, B-001).

limitations: Simulation only: a pump and a balance with a simple physical model (0.4 % pump CV, 0.1 mg balance noise). Not a calibrated instrument model.
The Compose service has not been built yet; CI's compose job will build it on the next approved push.

features.title: Hardware Hub: environments, devices and capabilities registry
features.description: A workspace connects environments chosen from the operator's catalog (PAP_ENVIRONMENTS); discovery records each device, its description digest and its capabilities; properties can be read live. Observation only for physical environments (D-026).
acceptance: Workspaces can connect only environments the operator configured; the API never contacts a URL a user supplied.

Discovery against the real virtual laboratory records every device with its capabilities, input/output schemas and description digest; re-discovery marks vanished devices missing instead of deleting them.
A property is read live from the device through the API.
Another organization's environments and devices are 404; connecting needs admin, discovery needs engineer.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_hardware.py: 6 passed against the real lab: catalog-only connection (a URL in the body is ignored), discovery of 3 devices with schemas and 64-hex digests, unchanged re-discovery (3,0,0,0), a vanished device kept and marked missing, live reads, roles (viewer/engineer/admin), a withdrawn environment answers 409.

test_isolation.py: 4 passed; the victim now has an environment, discovered devices, a workflow and a run; every org route (enumerated from OpenAPI) is attacked by an outsider user and an outsider service credential, including IDOR with the attacker's own org; all 404, nothing leaked.
verify.sh full: 201 pytest passed (engine required), migrations 0004/0005 without drift (test_scaffold).

limitations: Physical environments are discovery and read only by design (D-026).
Operator catalog changes need a restart (settings are read at start).

features.title: Durable simulated workflow execution with an engine-verified result
features.description: Workflows are ordered device actions plus a verification contract. Runs execute in the worker with a PostgreSQL lease, a step journal written before each dispatch, and the verified result from openmhs outcome verify (D-028).
acceptance: A run executes its steps in order in the worker, each journalled before and after dispatch; the API never dispatches.
Before every command the executor checks that the environment is configured simulated and that the device reports simulated=true; otherwise the step fails and nothing is sent.
A worker killed mid-run is replaced and the run finishes; a repeated idempotent step has one physical effect; a non-idempotent step left in flight stops as outcome_unknown instead of being re-sent.

The verified result comes from the real pinned engine (outcome verify) on an RFC 0004 contract with the balance reading as independent evidence; with an injected fault the pump reports success and the engine returns VIOLATED.
Reported and verified outcomes are stored and shown separately.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_workflows.py (PAP_REQUIRE_ENGINE=1): 7 passed with the real pinned engine and the real lab.
API only queues (all steps pending after POST); healthy run: reported succeeded, engine SATISFIED, supported_success, provenance carries the engine commit from engine.lock.json.
Injected partial_blockage: pump reports success, engine VIOLATED, outcome class contradiction.
Environment configured physical: step refused before any dispatch (dispatches 0); the lab's own invocation list shows no tare was received.

Crash simulations: a non-idempotent step left in flight ends outcome_unknown and is not re-sent (invocation count unchanged); an idempotent step is re-sent with the same request id and takes effect once (one 200 µL dose on the balance, verdict SATISFIED).

A real worker process is hard-killed mid-run (after tare and two of eight doses); a new worker resumes after the 5 s lease; attempts 2; the balance shows 8 x 20 µL within 2 % (a repeated dose would add 12.5 %); verdict SATISFIED.

limitations: One template (dispense-and-verify); custom definitions are accepted as JSON, there is no editor canvas.
Run cancellation is not implemented.
Timestamps in the evidence are the worker's clock at the device's answer (50 ms uncertainty declared), not the instrument's own clock.

features.title: Physical AI Workbench
features.description: The signature workspace: devices on the left, the run and live instrument state in the centre, an inspector (step input/output, evidence, verdict, provenance) on the right, the run timeline below; resizable; from real backend data only.
acceptance: Starting a workflow, following its steps and reading its reported and verified result all happen on one page, from the API.
Selecting a step shows its request, the device's answer, timing and, for the verification, the engine's conditions and observed values.
Panels resize by pointer and keyboard; the page passes the axe gate in both themes.

evidence: e2e/lab.spec.ts (smoke.sh --e2e, 2026-11-21): a run started from the Workbench button is executed by the worker and shown live to Supported success with the step timeline; an injected blockage shows reported succeeded with reported_dispensed_ul = 100 beside the engine's violated verdict; the inspector separator resizes by keyboard (340 -> 356 -> Home 260).
e2e/a11y.spec.ts: the Workbench (with a finished run), Hardware Hub, Workflows and Get started pages pass axe-core WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A/AA in the dark and the light theme with zero violations.

limitations: No 3D viewport, no telemetry plots, no engineering assistant: not built and not shown.
Live instrument values are polled every 1.5 s through the API, not streamed.

features.title: First-run onboarding: workspace, environment, discovery, first verified run
features.description: Milestone: a new user registers a simulated instrument, discovers its capabilities, executes a workflow and receives a verified result entirely through the interface.
acceptance: A signed-in user without a workspace is led to create one, choose an environment from the catalog and discover its devices; progress is derived from server data, not browser storage.
A browser test does the whole path as a new user: sign in, create workspace, connect the virtual laboratory, discover, run the dispense-and-verify workflow, read the engine-verified result.
No step of the path needs the API, a terminal or the repository.

evidence: e2e/lab.spec.ts 'a new user goes from sign-in to an engine-verified result through the interface only' (32.5 s): sign in, create workspace, connect the virtual laboratory from the catalog, discover, create the workflow from a form generated from the template's schema, run, read reported succeeded / engine satisfied / Supported success, open the run in the Workbench (engine version, commit and binary digest shown), inspect the dispense step, read a live property in the Hardware Hub. The test makes no API call itself.
Onboarding progress is derived from server data (workspaces, environments, devices, workflows, runs); nothing is kept in browser storage.

limitations: Run on this machine's local stack; the Docker trial path has the lab service but has not been exercised end to end on CI yet.
No external user has done this; that is the separate external-adoption milestone.
